mechanism_narrative: A lower level of the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is associated with higher S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, as lower rates reduce the discount rate for equity valuations.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS level shows no significant correlation with 20-day returns (Rank IC < 0.03) over a 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 5.0% signals a tight labor market, which typically precedes stronger corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When UNRATE falls below 5.0%, the S&P 500 fails to produce positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of such instances.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in housing starts (HOUST) and GDP growth (GDPC1) indicates a robust economic expansion, which drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days through improved corporate revenue outlook.
failure_condition: The interaction between HOUST and GDPC1 (measured by their product) fails to predict positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of cases when both series show positive momentum.

mechanism_narrative: In a high inflation regime (CPIAUCSL above 3.0% year-over-year), a rising CPIAUCSL signals potential monetary tightening, which depresses equity valuations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods when CPIAUCSL exceeds 3.0% YoY, the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of instances despite rising CPI.

mechanism_narrative: A rising industrial production index (INDPRO) indicates robust manufacturing activity, which typically supports corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: INDPRO growth shows no significant positive correlation with 5-day returns (Rank IC < 0.03) over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in retail sales (RSAFS) below 600,000 million dollars signals weakening consumer demand, which typically precedes lower corporate revenues and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: When RSAFS falls below 600,000 million dollars, the S&P 500 fails to produce negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of such instances.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in employment (PAYEMS) and decrease in unemployment (UNRATE) indicates a strong labor market, which boosts consumer spending and corporate profits, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The interaction between PAYEMS growth and UNRATE decline (measured by their product) fails to predict positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of cases when both series show the expected direction.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS rising above 4.0% and sustained), an increase in the federal funds rate signals reduced liquidity and higher borrowing costs, which depresses equity valuations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods of sustained monetary tightening (FEDFUNDS > 4.0% for at least 3 months), the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances.
